label: rem:two-tier-scaling-pq
title: Two-tier scaling of $P_K(q)$: quantum dimension $[N]_q$ (topological) and base mass $m_0$ (physical)
html:
Remark (two-tier scaling of the confined Laurent polynomial P_K(q)). The map from a braid word to a physical mass passes through two logically separate scaling factors. We separate topological constants (intrinsic to the Hecke trace) from dimensional constants (set by the choice of physical anchor).

Tier 1: topological scaling — quantum dimension [N]_q

Before the Markov trace (categorical mass as Markov trace) qualifies as an isotopy invariant on the closure \hat{\beta}, the raw graded Euler characteristic of the braid word must be normalised so that an unbraided strand contributes a factor independent of the ambient brane content. That normalising factor is the quantum dimension of the fundamental fibre,

  [N]_q
  \;=\;
  \frac{q^{N} - q^{-N}}{q - q^{-1}}.

In Hecke language, [N]_q is the Markov-trace normalisation that ensures invariance under stabilisation \beta \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} (axiomatic Markov closed form). Physically, it acts as a vacuum subtraction: P_K(q) measures the excess topological complexity of the knot K relative to the unbraided substrate, not the absolute count of strands. Without this normalisation the polynomial would grow with every additional trivial component, and Reidemeister-I invariance would fail (Reidemeister mass invariance).

Tier 2: physical scaling — base mass m_0

Evaluating the normalised P_K(q) at the substrate parameter q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps) produces a dimensionless real number; converting to MeV requires multiplication by a base mass scale,

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{K}} \;\approx\; m_0 \cdot \bigl| P_K(q_0) \bigr|.

The choice of m_0 is a boundary condition of the framework, not a derivation. Three natural anchors appear in the literature:

Anchor Value Setting
Leptonic mass m_e \approx 0.511\;\mathrm{MeV} adopted by QOU as CAL-1 (calibration inputs)
Higgs VEV v \approx 246\;\mathrm{GeV} electroweak-localised models
Planck mass M_{\mathrm{Pl}} \approx 1.22 \times 10^{19}\;\mathrm{GeV} spacetime-fabric models

QOU selects m_0 = m_e on empirical grounds: m_e is the most precisely measured particle mass in the Standard Model, and the leptonic brane tower is fully computable from q_0 alone via m_e(\text{natural}) = \mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2})/\hbar_q^2 (three calibration inputs). The electroweak (v) and Planck (M_{\mathrm{Pl}}) choices correspond to different fibre-functor normalisations and produce algebraically equivalent predictions for dimensionless ratios such as m_\mu/m_e and m_n - m_p, but require independent calibration of the leptonic sector to match observed masses.

Significance of the separation

The two tiers commute with disjoint operations:

  • [N]_q acts inside the trace (Tier 1 is a categorical normalisation; it depends only on the rank N of the fundamental fibre and on q).
  • m_0 acts outside the trace (Tier 2 is a unit conversion; it has dimensions of mass and is independent of the braid word).

Mixing the two — for instance, by absorbing a power of [N]_q into m_0 — would make m_0 depend on the local Wedderburn channel and break the parameter count of three calibration inputs. The volume-density factorisation \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) \cdot \rho_q (Kashaev volume density) inherits the same separation: \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 is Tier-1 (topological, substrate-only), while the conversion of \mathfrak{m} to MeV is Tier-2 (physical, set by m_e).

Summary

The substrate-bound polynomial P_K(q) is a dimensionless topological multiplier; its Markov normalisation by [N]_q is fixed by the categorical structure, while the conversion to a macroscopic mass requires a separate dimensional anchor m_0 chosen by calibration (three calibration discipline). QOU pins m_0 = m_e; the Higgs-VEV and Planck-mass choices are mathematically admissible alternatives that re-route the calibration through the electroweak or gravitational sector respectively.
